hypothesis: The W-R27 near-chance binary future-delta task may reflect poor learned features rather than a total absence of next-step causal structure. Compare exact fixed causal first/second finite-difference numerical predictors and frozen development-selected recurrence on unseen raw observations.
data: W-R20 original four-channel byte sequence, offset79 and independent deterministic per-tick amplitudes 1,3,5. At time t in 2..14 only observed bytes at t,t-1,t-2 available for predictors. Evaluate against observed next byte at t+1 (never a feature).
predictors: development_selected: choose among first three using lowest aggregate circular absolute error on development affine/quadratic amp1/3; fixed for all heldout generators and amplitudes
selection: Tie-break persistence then velocity then acceleration; one global model choice, not per hidden generator or heldout condition.
metrics: Per generator/noise amplitude and all 4 channels, heldout circular absolute error (min modular byte distance) plus exact-byte and within8 accuracy; independently report each deterministic predictor.
classification: STRUCTURED_FORECAST if velocity affine MAE is at least8 bytes better than persistence and acceleration quadratic MAE is at least8 bytes better than velocity on heldout amp3; PARTIAL if either improves by at least8 but strict not met; NEGATIVE otherwise. Preserve negative xorshift behavior.
controls: Same input stream and future-label separation across arms, no target access during prediction
Frozen development-selection only; no hidden capacity or post-hoc choice
Exact source/prereg SHA, first-use archive and full Go test/build
No accepted-ref mutation, no model calls or retries
claim_limit: Deterministic raw byte forecasting diagnostic, not learned general intelligence.
